title: Ransomware and Cyber-Enabled Proceeds
summary: How ransomware and other cyber-enabled crimes generate proceeds, how payments are made and laundered, and how investigators trace and seek to recover them.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How ransomware and other cyber-enabled crimes generate proceeds, how payments are made and laundered, and how investigators trace and seek to recover them.
Learning Objectives: Explain the ransomware business model and payment process
Trace ransom payments and their laundering through crypto-asset channels
Coordinate with victims, incident responders and service providers
Syllabus: Ransom payments, reporting and engagement with victims
Laundering and cash-out of crypto-asset proceeds
Intended Audience: Fraud, economic crime and cybercrime investigators
FIU analysts handling fraud-related reports and urgent requests
Victim liaison, prevention and disruption officers working with the financial sector
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, cybercrime or financial crime investigation is helpful. No technical background in cyber security or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2023), Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-Enabled Fraud
FATF (2022), Partnering in the Fight Against Financial Crime: Data Protection, Technology and Private Sector Information Sharing
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
